module_title: Important Articles - Rights, Welfare, and Specific Provisions
introduction: At this level, we look at articles that define specific freedoms, protections against exploitation, educational rights, and crucial welfare directives given to the state.

core_concepts.title: Formation of New States (Article 3)
core_concepts.description: Article 3 empowers the Parliament to form a new state, increase or diminish the area of any state, and alter the boundaries or name of any state.

core_concepts.title: Discrimination vs. Opportunity (Art 15 & 16)
core_concepts.description: Article 15 prohibits discrimination ONLY on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth. Article 16 provides equality of opportunity specifically in matters of 'Public Employment' (government jobs).

core_concepts.title: The Six Freedoms (Article 19)
core_concepts.description: Guarantees 6 freedoms: Speech & expression, Assembly, Association, Movement, Residence, and Profession. (The right to acquire property was deleted from here by the 44th Amendment).

core_concepts.title: Right to Education (Article 21A)
core_concepts.description: Added by the 86th Amendment Act, 2002. It declares that the State shall provide free and compulsory education to all children of the age of 6 to 14 years.

core_concepts.title: Exploitation & Labour (Art 23 & 24)
core_concepts.description: Article 23 prohibits human trafficking and forced labour (begar). Article 24 prohibits the employment of children below the age of 14 years in factories, mines, or hazardous activities.

core_concepts.title: Important DPSPs
core_concepts.description: Art 39A: Free legal aid to the poor. Art 45: Early childhood care and education for children below 6 years. Art 48A: Protection of the environment, forests, and wildlife. Art 50: Separation of judiciary from executive.

important_entities.name: Article 19(1)(a)
important_entities.significance: The 'Freedom of Press' is not explicitly mentioned anywhere in the Constitution. The Supreme Court has ruled that it is implicitly covered under the freedom of speech and expression in Article 19.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Not all Fundamental Rights are available to foreigners. Articles 15, 16, 19, 29, and 30 are available ONLY to citizens of India.
Art 21 is Right to Life. Art 21A is Right to Education (6-14 years). Art 45 is a DPSP directing the state to care for children below 6 years. Do not confuse them.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Speech, Assembly, Association, Movement, Residence, Profession.

exam_strategy_tips: Article 48A (Environment) and 39A (Free Legal Aid) were added by the 42nd Amendment. Exams often ask which DPSPs were added later.
Matching questions often pair Art 50 with 'Separation of Judiciary' and Art 44 with 'Uniform Civil Code'.
